stories.title: FBI Top-10 cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro' captured in Sinaloa raid that killed 11
stories.summary: Mexican forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, one of the FBI's 10 most-wanted fugitives, in a Friday-night raid in Guasave, Sinaloa, and flew him to Mexico City with two top lieutenants. The operation, aided by U.S. intelligence, killed four soldiers and seven suspected gunmen and set off burning roadblocks - and experts warn picking off capos could trigger another wave of faction violence.

stories.title: Ballistic missile attack on Zelenskyy's hometown Kryvyi Rih kills 2, wounds 60
stories.summary: A Russian strike on the centre of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown killed two people and wounded 60 others, local officials said Saturday. The attack added to uncertainty over Washington-brokered peace efforts and came hours after two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland.

stories.title: UN talks end with softened pledge to draft 'killer robot' rules by 2028
stories.summary: Week-long UN talks in Geneva ended Saturday with only a softened pledge to develop rules for lethal autonomous weapons by 2028, after Russian opposition blocked binding commitments. Human-rights groups, who had wanted legally binding rules quickly, called the outcome deeply disappointing.

stories.title: Russian cargo ship ablaze in Baltic after drone strike; Finland tightens security
stories.summary: The Sparta II, a US-sanctioned Russian cargo ship with defence-industry links, was hit by drones in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, caught fire and drifted into Finnish waters; Finland called it a likely Ukrainian attack and imposed temporary air and maritime restrictions. The 16-member crew evacuated safely - the latest sign of the Ukraine war spilling toward NATO territory.

stories.title: Two groups verify mathematician's claim that Claude helped prove the Riemann hypothesis
stories.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpoege's claim that he proved the Riemann hypothesis - one of math's most famous open problems - with the help of Claude now has two independent verifications, the Guardian reports. Alpoege released the work Friday as roughly 17 million lines of formal Lean proof code, and independent checkers have now certified that it compiles and the headline theorems hold.

stories.title: Thinking Machines opens weights of Inkling 2 Mini, a 26B model that runs on laptops
stories.summary: Thinking Machines released open weights for Inkling 2 Mini, a 26B-parameter looped mixture-of-experts model that reads text and images and is sized to run on laptops, with ready-made quantized builds from Unsloth. It makes private, offline AI prototyping practical - though no benchmarks or license details have been published yet.

stories.title: The AI boom had a bad week - Nasdaq's worst since 2020, S&P and Dow in correction
stories.summary: AI stocks had their worst week since the COVID crash: the Nasdaq fell 10%, the S&P 500 and Dow entered correction territory, and Anthropic's IPO ended near its offer price, fueling fears of a bursting AI bubble. Because AI names now anchor index funds and retirement portfolios, a sustained unwind would ripple well beyond tech.

stories.title: Browns bye-week roundup: Colts cut Daniel Jones, Drake Maye breaks leg
stories.summary: On Day 3 of the Browns' bye, the OBR newswire tracks the wild-card race around them: Indianapolis cut QB Daniel Jones 11 games into his $88 million deal (about $50M paid, $35.2M dead cap next year), and Drake Maye's broken leg hits 5-5 New England - the club directly ahead of Cleveland in the playoff standings. The Rams' first-round pick from the Myles Garrett trade also gains value as 6-4 Los Angeles faces a brutal closing schedule.

stories.title: Saturday Dawg Chow: a slow bye-week sports Saturday
stories.summary: With the Browns on their bye, the Saturday Dawg Chow rounds up the weekend's notes - including a franchise-history interview with former safety Thom Darden, who spent a decade making receivers think twice about crossing Cleveland's secondary.

stories.title: Jeremiah Smith sets Big Ten record with 18th career 100-yard game
stories.summary: Jeremiah Smith's first half at Nebraska - four catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns - was the 18th 100-yard receiving game of his career, breaking the Big Ten record he had shared with Michigan's Braylon Edwards and Purdue's David Bell. And he set the mark before halftime of a game the 7-3 Buckeyes need to keep their faint playoff hopes alive.

stories.title: Jeremiah Smith ties Terry Glenn's Ohio State single-season receiving TD record
stories.summary: Smith's second touchdown against Nebraska - a 31-yard catch at the back of the end zone - was his 17th receiving score of the season, tying Terry Glenn's 1995 Ohio State single-season record. He is now two short of Desmond Howard's Big Ten single-season mark of 19, with Michigan still on the schedule.

stories.title: Fahey hits Smith for 67-yard TD on opening drive; Ryan Day penalty doesn't negate it
stories.summary: Backup quarterback Luke Fahey connected with Jeremiah Smith for a 67-yard touchdown on the opening drive at Nebraska, and a sideline-interference flag against Ryan Day did not negate the score. The quick strike carried over the momentum from last week's win over Northwestern, with injured starter Julian Sayin watching.

stories.title: What's next for injured Ohio State QB Julian Sayin?
stories.summary: Injured quarterback Julian Sayin (throwing-arm injury) missed a fourth straight game Saturday at Nebraska and could sit the rest of the regular season. The Dispatch examines his options: he has two years of eligibility left, and with backup Luke Fahey struggling to push the ball downfield, a healthy Sayin would likely reclaim the starting job in 2027 if he returns.

stories.title: Antonelli fastest in Vegas qualifying but Verstappen inherits pole
stories.summary: Newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli set the fastest time in Las Vegas Grand Prix qualifying but drops to sixth with a five-place grid penalty, handing pole to Max Verstappen for Saturday night's race down the Strip. With both championships already decided, the tight fight for runner-up in the drivers' standings - five drivers within 33 points - is what remains to play for.

stories.title: Driver dies after crashing stolen vehicle while fleeing police on Northeast Side
stories.summary: A driver died after crashing a reported stolen vehicle while fleeing police on the Northeast Side. Officers first tried to stop the car near Neil and Buttles around 12:35 a.m.; the driver fled, lost control on Hudson Street and struck a pole, and was pronounced dead at the scene.

stories.title: Columbus weather: a mild weekend before temperatures trend cooler
stories.summary: Central Ohio gets one more mild day - mostly sunny with a high near 67 - before a cold front brings late showers Sunday and knocks Monday back to about 50. The chill holds into Thanksgiving week, with scattered showers possible on Thanksgiving Day and highs in the low-to-mid 40s.

stories.title: Columbus community leaders demand comprehensive affordable-housing action plan
stories.summary: Columbus Urban League President Stephanie Hightower says the group has fielded more than 12,000 housing-distress calls since July - about 3,000 a month - as community leaders including the Columbus NAACP demand a comprehensive affordable-housing action plan with wraparound services from city and county officials. Hightower likens the city's housing crunch to a crisis on par with COVID-19.

stories.title: State Rep. Munira Abdullahi launches Columbus mayoral campaign from the left
stories.summary: State Rep. Munira Abdullahi of Northland formally launched a Columbus mayoral campaign Saturday, running to the left of Mayor Andrew Ginther and Council President Shannon Hardin and seeking the local DSA's endorsement - a first for a Columbus mayoral candidate. If elected, the 30-year-old Somali American would be the city's first female, first Muslim and first foreign-born mayor; the nonpartisan primary is May 4.
